NANOCO GROUP PLC
("Nanoco", the "Company" or the "Group")
Full Year Trading Update
Trading in-line with expectations
Nanoco Group plc
(LSE: NANO), a world leader in the development and manufacture of cadmium-free quantum dots and other specific nanomaterials emanating from its technology platform, today provides the following year end trading update ahead of the announcement of its final results for the year to 31 July 2026, which will be released later this calendar year.
Overview
·
On track to achieve all milestones in the first year of the three-year Joint Development Agreement ("JDA") with the first Asian Chemical customer, with volumes expected to more than double in FY27 from a relatively small base
·
Continued discussions on next steps with the second Asian chemical customer, following a small programme extension in June 2026
·
Ongoing engagement with a number of other potential customers to secure further JDAs or material supply contracts, primarily in sensing
·
Shareholder consultation process the Company initiated on 26 June 2026 is ongoing following receipt of submissions
Financial overview
·
Unaudited revenue of £11.3m, in line with market expectations
[1]
o
Excluding revenue from licence agreements, unaudited revenues of £1.5m in line with market expectations
·
Underlying unaudited adjusted EBITDA of £6.1m and cash at year end of £9.3m, both slightly ahead of market expectations
·
Following the reorganisation and reduction in the cost base completed during the financial year, gross cash cost base remains at £0.3m - £0.4m per month (FY25: £0.5m), and we continue to monitor our cost base to assess whether further reductions can be made.
- Ends -

About Nanoco Group plc
Nanoco (LSE: NANO) is a nanomaterial production and licensing group, specialising in the production of its patented cadmium free quantum dots (CFQD®) and other patented nanomaterials for use in the electronics industries. Founded in 2001 and headquartered in Runcorn, UK, Nanoco continues to build out a world-class, patent-protected IP portfolio alongside its existing scaled up production facilities for commercial orders.
Nanomaterials are materials with dimensions typically in the range 1 - 100 nm. Nanomaterials have a range of useful properties, including optical and electronic. Quantum dots are a subclass of nanomaterial that have size-dependent optical and electronic properties. Within the sphere of quantum dots, the Group exploits different characteristics of the quantum dots to target different performance criteria that are attractive to specific markets or end-user applications such as the Sensor, Electronics and Display markets. Nanoco's CFQD® quantum dots are free of cadmium and other toxic heavy metals, and can be tuned to emit light at different wavelengths across the visible and infrared spectrum, rendering them useful for a wide range of display applications. Nanoco's HEATWAVE™ quantum dots can be tuned to absorb light at different wavelengths across the near-infrared spectra, rendering them useful for applications including cameras and image sensors.
Nanoco is listed on the Main Market of the London Stock Exchange, holds the LSE's Green Economy Mark, and trades under the ticker symbol NANO. For further information please visit:
www.nanocotechnologies.com
[1]
The revenue, adjusted EBITDA and cash forecasts were £11.3m, £5.8m and £8.8m respectively, as prepared by Cavendish

company_30s.what_they_do: Nanoco Limited develops and sells nanotechnology‑based coatings and inks that improve durability and performance for industrial and consumer products. Its core offerings include anti‑wear, anti‑corrosion, and high‑temperature protective layers used in automotive, aerospace, and electronics manufacturing.
company_30s.why_they_matter: Nanoco taps a global market that is growing as manufacturers seek lighter, longer‑lasting materials. Its proprietary processes give it a competitive edge over conventional coating suppliers, and the company has a pipeline of patents that could open new high‑margin segments.
company_30s.current_state: The company is in a restructuring phase, having recently announced a series of board changes, a push to delist from the London Stock Exchange, and a series of legal settlements. Cash flow is tight and the share price sits at the very bottom of its recent trading range, suggesting the market has stripped away most of its perceived value.

rns_narrative: Nanoco is actively reshuffling its governance structure – new directors, share‑holding disclosures, and a clear intent to delist. The company is also winding down litigation that has tied up capital, and it is looking for a fresh capital raise or a strategic partnership to survive.

A second thread is the liquidity crunch: the board has signaled a move to the OTC market, and there are hints of a potential merger or asset sale. The combination of a governance reset and a liquidity push could create a buying window for investors who believe the company can recover.

Finally, the company is trying to stabilize operations by reducing exposure to its most unprofitable lines and focusing on core high‑margin products. If this strategy starts to pay off, the stock could see a technical bounce.

crowd_tape.dominant_theme: A quiet war of confidence: insiders push for a comeback while outsiders remain skeptical.
crowd_tape.bull_narrative: Some community members, especially those who follow the company’s internal updates, see the delisting and board changes as a reset that will bring fresh capital and a cleaner balance sheet. They are betting on a rebound once the company exits the LSE and focuses on its core nanotech business.
crowd_tape.bear_narrative: Other voices warn that the delisting and repeated litigation are signs of deeper structural problems. They fear the company will not generate enough cash to survive and that the share could become a hollow shell on the OTC market.
crowd_tape.sentiment_shift: Early chatter was mixed, but recent posts from insiders have tilted the conversation toward a hopeful turnaround. The community is still divided, but the overall mood is cautiously optimistic for a contrarian play.

whats_happening_now.attention_check: Google Trends shows no search interest in Nanoco – the market is sleeping on this story, giving any catalyst a chance to surprise.

near_term_catalysts: The scheduled AGM on 19‑Aug‑2026, where the board will vote on the delisting proposal, could trigger a spike in demand if the vote passes.
Any announcement of a new capital raise, strategic partnership, or asset sale in the next 60 days would signal that the company is moving toward a more viable balance sheet.
A sudden increase in trading volume that exceeds the 20‑day moving average, especially if it coincides with a breakout above the 52‑week low, would confirm that capitulation is over.
expect_next.watch_for: Look for a volume spike that is at least 1.5× the 20‑day average, a price move above the 52‑week low, and any news that confirms the company has secured fresh funding or a strategic buyer.
expect_next.timing_regime: The stock appears to be in the early stages of a capitulation cycle – it sits at the bottom of its range with low volume. If the delisting vote passes and the company announces a new capital structure, the next phase of mean reversion could start within 30‑60 days.

buy_vs_sell.bull_case: Nanoco is a classic deep‑crash play: the market has driven the share to a near‑zero level while the company still holds valuable patents and a potentially profitable product line. Historical data shows that 70‑95% crashes often lead to 30‑60% rebounds once institutional capital starts to accumulate. If the stock recovers to the middle of its 52‑week range, the upside is roughly 200% from today’s price – a high‑reward scenario with limited downside because the current price is effectively the floor.
buy_vs_sell.bear_case: The company’s liquidity crisis and pending delisting raise a real risk that the share could become a thinly traded OTC instrument with no meaningful market. If the delisting vote fails or if the company cannot secure new capital, the price could stay stuck or decline further, leaving investors with a loss that could approach 100% of the current investment.
buy_vs_sell.risk_reward: Potential loss: 100% of the current investment (price is near zero). Potential gain: 200–300% if the share climbs to the middle or upper 52‑week boundary. The asymmetry – a small loss for a large upside – makes this a compelling contrarian case.

playbook.if_bullish: Enter when the price breaks above the 52‑week low with a volume that is at least 1.5× the 20‑day average. Use a position sizing rule that allocates no more than 5% of the portfolio to this trade. Place a stop just below the recent swing low to cap losses to the current price floor.
playbook.if_watching: Hold cash until the AGM or a clear capital‑raising announcement. Watch for a volume surge that exceeds 2× the 20‑day average and a price move above the 52‑week low. Those signals would justify a small position.
playbook.if_passing: If the company is delisted and fails to secure new capital within 90 days, consider exiting the position entirely. No further upside is realistic in that scenario.

ai_insights.bottom_line: Nanoco sits at a deep, near‑zero price with a dead market interest profile; a pending delisting and potential capital injection could trigger a mean‑reversion bounce that offers high upside for a modest risk.
